quirks: The 1890 federal census was destroyed — no coverage exists for North Dakota; the 1900 census (92% name-indexed on FamilySearch) is the earliest reliable federal census.

Statewide birth and death registration began in 1907 with full compliance by 1924 (FS Wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/North_Dakota_Vital_Records). County-level birth records in Benson County started in the late 1890s; county death records from 1895. An 1898 birth may appear in county records but not in any statewide series.
Statewide marriage registration began in 1925. Pre-1925 marriages are in county-level records; FamilySearch collection 2550852 (County Marriages, 1872-2000) covers Benson County.

Lutheran church records are particularly important for this region — Scandinavian (Norwegian) immigrants were prominent in Benson County. Flora and Esmond area Lutheran church volumes are digitized on FamilySearch (DGS 100881427 and 100881428) but are only 34-36% indexed — browse required for full coverage.
Benson County Clerk of District Court holds birth records from the late 1890s, marriage records from the late 1800s, and death/probate/court records from 1895.
The 1915 North Dakota state census is available on FamilySearch (collection 2346284, index & images) and covers Benson County.
Search neighboring counties — Eddy, Nelson, Pierce, Ramsey, Towner, and Wells — as families near county lines commonly generated records on both sides.

Naturalization records for Benson County District Court (1884-1955) are digitized on FamilySearch as full-text searchable volumes but are 0% name-indexed — use full-text search or browse. These can name a declarant's wife and children and are a strong indirect parentage source if the father was an immigrant.
No courthouse disaster is recorded for Benson County — records are expected to be intact.
Spirit Lake (Devils Lake) Indian Reservation is located in Benson County; Fort Totten Indian Agency records (1881-1945) are separately digitized on FamilySearch if Native ancestry is relevant.
entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Research Guide: Benson County, North Dakota (1890–1920)

## Jurisdictional History
Benson County was organized 9 March 1883 from DeSmet and Ramsey Counties (Dakota Territory). North Dakota became a state 2 November 1889; from that point the county is filed as Benson, North Dakota. County seat: Minnewaukan. Neighboring counties: Eddy, Nelson, Pierce, Ramsey, Towner, Wells.

## Vital Records
| Type | County Level Starts | Statewide Level Starts | Full Compliance |
|------|---------------------|-----------------------|-----------------|
| Birth | Late 1890s | 1907 | 1924 |
| Death | 1895 | 1907 | 1924 |
| Marriage | Late 1800s | 1925 | — |

*Source: [North Dakota Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/North_Dakota_Vital_Records); [Benson County, North Dakota Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Benson_County,_North_Dakota_Genealogy)*

An 1898 birth like Reuben's falls in the county-level-only window. Statewide certificates did not begin until 1907. **The Benson County Clerk of District Court (311 B Ave Street, Minnewaukan, ND 58351, 701-473-5345) is the primary repository for any county-filed birth record from this period.** FamilySearch Library has not acquired ND birth or death records.

### Marriage Records Online
- **1872–2000**: [North Dakota, County Marriages](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2550852) at FamilySearch — index & images
- [Benson County Marriage Announcements](http://genealogytrails.com/ndak/benson/news_marriages.html) (Genealogy Trails)

## Census Records
- **1890 federal census destroyed** — no coverage for North Dakota.
- **1900 federal census** — 92% name-indexed on FamilySearch (DGS 004120517); Reuben born 1898 would appear as ~age 1-2 in parental household. **Primary target.**
- **1910 federal census** — available and indexed on FamilySearch.
- **1915 ND state census** — [FamilySearch collection 2346284](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2346284), index & images; 51–55% indexed (two Benson County volumes: DGS 007637091, 007637092).
- **1925 ND state census** — [FamilySearch collection 2351024](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2351024), index & images.

## Church Records
Scandinavian (particularly Norwegian) Lutheran immigrants dominated much of Benson County. Church baptismal registers naming parents are a primary parentage source when civil records are sparse.
- **Flora Lutheran Church** (DGS 100881427, 712 images, 1820–1997) — 34% indexed, English/Norwegian. Browse required.
- **Esmond area church records** (DGS 100881428, 396 images, 1830–1958) — 36% indexed, English/Norwegian. Browse required.
- **ELCA Records 1875–1940** at Ancestry ($) — [collection 60722](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60722/).

## Naturalization Records
If Reuben's father was an immigrant, his Declaration of Intention or Petition for Naturalization often named wife and children — strong indirect parentage evidence.
- **Benson County District Court naturalization volumes** (1884–1955) — 5 digitized volume sets on FamilySearch, 0% name-indexed but **full-text searchable**. Use FamilySearch full-text search.
- **[North Dakota, Naturalization Records, 1868–1924](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3241359)** at FamilySearch — index & images.
- **[North Dakota and South Dakota Naturalization Records, 1851–1924](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3241319)** at FamilySearch.

## Land & Homestead Records
Many Benson County families arrived as homesteaders in the 1880s–1900s. Land records can establish when a family arrived and link to other records.
- [BLM General Land Office Records](https://glorecords.blm.gov/) — homestead patent index, some images
- [Benson County BLM Land Records Index](http://www.usgwarchives.net/nd/benson/bensland.html) at USGenWeb Archives

## Pioneer & Immigration Files
- **[Red River Valley Genealogical Society, Pioneer Files, 1880–1953](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3155904)** at FamilySearch — compiled biographical files on early settlers; index.

## Cemetery Records
- **[North Dakota, Cemetery Records, 1877–1999](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1451475)** at FamilySearch — index & images
- [FindAGrave — Benson County](https://www.findagrave.com/cemetery-browse/USA/North-Dakota/Benson-County?id=county_1753)

## Newspapers & Obituaries
- [Chronicling America](http://chroniclingamerica.loc.gov/) — some ND digitized newspapers free
- [Genealogy Trails — Benson County Obituaries](http://genealogytrails.com/ndak/benson/obits.html)
- [NDGenWeb Obituaries](http://sites.rootsweb.com/~ndbenso2/obits/Obits.htm)
- GenealogyBank ($), NewspaperArchive ($)

## Probate Records
- Probate records at Benson County Clerk of District Court from 1883.
- **[North Dakota and South Dakota Wills and Probate Records, 1800–1985](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/9081)** at Ancestry ($)

## Neighboring Counties to Search
Check Eddy, Nelson, Pierce, Ramsey, Towner, and Wells counties — families near borders commonly generated records on multiple sides.

## Key Repositories
- **Benson County Courthouse**, 311 B Ave Street, Minnewaukan, ND 58351 (701-473-5345) — birth, marriage, death, court, probate records
- **State Historical Society of North Dakota / State Archives** — [history.nd.gov/archives](http://history.nd.gov/archives/genealogy.html)
- **North Dakota State University Archives** — biography index, obituary index, naturalization index
- **FamilySearch Centers**: Grand Forks ND, Minot ND; Lake Region Public Library (affiliate)

fields.transcription:
Riverside Reuben Spriggs

Services for Reuben Spencer Spriggs, 99, were Monday at Acheson & Graham Garden of Prayer Mortuary in Riverside. He died of congestive heart failure May 21 at Palm Terrace Convalescent Center in Riverside.

Burial will be Monday at De Smet Cemetery in De Smet, S. D.

Acheson and Graham Garden of Prayer Mortuary in Riverside is handling arrangements.

Mr. Spriggs, who was born in Maddock, N. D., lived in Riverside for three years. He was a farmer.

He is survived by two daughters, Dona Darwin of Riverside and Karen Quass of Roseville, Minn.; and a son, Spencer Spriggs Jr.

Question: q_001 — "Who were the parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs, born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota?"

NAMING DISCREPANCY requiring formal resolution:

Three records name Reuben Spencer Spriggs's father with different given-name forms:

RECORD 1 — 1910 US Census (src_003, log_011)
Father listed as: "John W Spriggs" — head of household, Male, married, born 1872, Iowa. Wife: Charlotte Spriggs, born 1877, Norway. At Prairie Belle Township, Beadle County, South Dakota. Children: Rueben S Spriggs (b.1899 ND), Lillian F Spriggs (b.1900 Iowa), Leonard W Spriggs (b.1907 SD). Explicit ParentChild relationship indexed for Rueben S Spriggs.

RECORD 2 — WWI Draft Registration Card, 12 Sep 1918 (src_001, log_012)
Reuben Spencer Spriggs (registrant) names: "Father - Wm Spriggs" as nearest relative, address #1 Esmond, S.D. Also identifies employer as "self & help father Wm Spriggs."

RECORD 3 — 1920 US Census (src_004, log_017)
Father listed as: "Will Spriggs" — head of household, Male, married, born 1873, Iowa. Wife: Charlott Spriggs, born 1878, Norway, imm. 1877. At Belle Prairie Township, Beadle County, South Dakota. Children: Spencer Spriggs (b.1899 ND = Reuben Spencer Spriggs), Leonard Spriggs (b.1907 SD). NO explicit ParentChild relationship in index (household-role evidence only).

ANALYSIS CONTEXT:
The three name forms are "John W," "Wm," and "Will." All three records share:
- Same wife (Charlotte/Charlott), Norwegian birth (~1877-1878), immigrated 1877
- Same son born ~1898-1899 in North Dakota (Rueben S / Spencer)
- Same younger son Leonard born 1907 in South Dakota
- Same location (Belle Prairie Township, Beadle County, South Dakota)
- Consistent Iowa birth for the father (~1872-1873)

The 1920 census definitively shows "Will Spriggs" in the same household configuration as 1910 "John W Spriggs," with Reuben Spencer Spriggs present as son in both. The registrant himself (Reuben) called his father "Wm Spriggs" in 1918 — a first-person identification. "Will" is a common nickname for "William." "Wm" is the standard abbreviation for "William." The "W" in "John W Spriggs" (1910) likely = William.

The "John" in 1910 may reflect: (a) his full legal name "John William Spriggs," or (b) a 1910 enumerator recording error. The 1920 enumerator and Reuben himself (1918) both use the William/Will form, suggesting "Will" was his preferred name.

Please create a conflict entry with formal weighing analysis and resolution. The resolution should document whether these three records refer to the same individual (they clearly do) and what his preferred/call name was (William/Will). This is needed before person-evidence can confidently link the "father" personas from all three records to a single new tree person.

entry.description: Father's given name: 'John W Spriggs' (1910 census, a_031) vs. 'Wm Spriggs' (1918 draft card, a_057) vs. 'Will Spriggs' (1920 census, a_069) — three name forms for the same head of household in Belle Prairie Township, Beadle County, SD
entry.independence_analysis: All three sources are independent. The 1910 census (src_003) was created by a county enumerator canvassing Belle Prairie Township — it does not derive from the draft card or the 1920 census. The 1918 WWI draft registration card (src_001) was completed by Reuben Spencer Spriggs personally at his local board in Beadle County — it is wholly independent of any census. The 1920 census (src_004) was compiled by a different enumerator a decade later and does not reference or derive from either prior source. Because each source was created by a different person (the 1910 enumerator, Reuben himself, the 1920 enumerator) at a different time, the three name forms represent three genuinely independent observations. There is no shared informant, no copying relationship, and no evidence any later recorder consulted an earlier record. The independence assessment therefore grants each source its full individual weight.
entry.weighing_analysis: Two decisive factors differentiate the three assertions. First, informant proximity: a_057 (draft card) records Reuben Spencer Spriggs's own hand — he named 'Wm Spriggs' as his nearest relative, his father. A son writing his own father's name is primary information; no one had closer or more reliable knowledge of the father's name. By contrast, a_031 (1910 enumerator) and a_069 (1920 enumerator) are both secondary — enumerators recorded names as spoken or remembered by whoever answered the door, and enumerator transcription errors for given names (recording legal first names instead of call names, or phonetic approximations) are a well-documented class of error in US census records. Second, internal consistency: 'Wm' (abbreviation for William) and 'Will' (nickname for William) agree on the underlying name — William — and differ only in abbreviation form. 'John W' is the outlier, but its 'W' middle initial aligns with William. The preponderance from two independent enumerators plus Reuben's own testimony is that the father's call name was William (Will/Wm); 'John' was likely a legal first name he did not use. Preferred assertion: a_057, Reuben's own primary testimony.
entry.resolution_rationale:
The dispute concerns the given name of Reuben Spencer Spriggs's father, who appears as 'John W Spriggs' in the 1910 Beadle County census, 'Wm Spriggs' on the 1918 WWI draft card, and 'Will Spriggs' in the 1920 Beadle County census. Resolving which form is correct matters because it is the name under which marriage and other records for the father must be searched.

The three assertions draw on independent sources. The 1910 census entry (a_031) was created by an enumerator recording the household in Belle Prairie Township — a secondary informant for the father's given name. The 1918 draft card (a_057) was completed in Reuben's own hand; he wrote 'Wm Spriggs' as his nearest relative. This is primary information: Reuben was a competent adult naming his own father, with no plausible reason for error on that specific detail. The 1920 census (a_069) records the same household under 'Will Spriggs,' with the same wife (Charlott, born Norway) and son (Spencer, b. 1899 ND) — a different enumerator, a decade later, corroborating the William form.

The preferred assertion is a_057. 'Wm' and 'Will' (a_069) both represent William and agree on the call name; 'John W' (a_031) is the outlier whose 'W' middle initial nonetheless confirms William as part of the name. The most likely explanation for 'John W' is the well-documented pattern in which US census enumerators recorded a man's legal first name rather than his call name: a man baptized or registered as 'John William' who went by 'Will' his entire life would appear in official documents under 'John' when an enumerator asked a neighbor or consulted a tax list, while family members and the man himself consistently used William. The 1910 enumerator recorded the legal form; Reuben and the 1920 enumerator recorded the call name. The conflict is resolved: the father's name was William (Will) Spriggs.

entry.description: Reuben Spencer Spriggs's birth year: 1898 (draft card a_003) vs. 1899 (1910 census a_026)
entry.independence_analysis: The two assertions draw on genuinely independent sources: a_003 comes from Reuben's own WWI draft registration card (original record, src_001), which was created in September 1918 and does not derive from any census. a_026 comes from the 1910 federal census (src_003), a separately enumerated record created in April 1910 by a different government process with a different informant. Neither source could have copied from the other. The sources are therefore independent, and each receives its individual evidential weight.
entry.weighing_analysis: The decisive factor is informant proximity. a_003 is Reuben's own handwritten statement on his draft card: he self-reported his birth date as '6 November 1898.' A registrant at age ~19 reporting his own birth date in a legal document has direct, self-interested knowledge. a_026 derives from the 1910 census, taken in April 1910, where an unidentified household member reported Reuben's age as 11 (from which birth year 1899 is calculated). A census birth-year figure is always derived from a stated age, not from a direct date report. The one-year discrepancy is wholly explained by enumeration timing: the 1910 census was taken in April, before Reuben's November birthday. A child born November 1898 was 11 years old in April 1910 — the enumerator records age 11, back-calculates birth year as 1910-11 = 1899, even though the actual birth year was 1898. This is a standard pre-1940 census age-to-year artifact, not a substantive disagreement about the birth year.
entry.resolution_rationale: The dispute is whether Reuben Spencer Spriggs was born in 1898 or 1899. The draft card (a_003) gives '6 November 1898' and the 1910 census (a_026) gives '1899' (derived from stated age 11). The draft card is the preferred evidence for three reasons. First, Reuben personally wrote and signed his draft card — he is the most reliable informant for his own birth date, and the specific day and month (6 November) shows genuine recollection rather than a rough estimate. Second, the 1910 census recorded only an age (11), not a birth date; the year 1899 is the enumerator's back-calculation and not what any informant stated. Third, the one-year discrepancy is fully explained by enumeration timing: the April 1910 census captured Reuben before his November birthday, making him age 11 even though he was born in November 1898 — the classic pre-1940 age-enumeration artifact. The 1898 date is corroborated by the subject's own 1998 obituary (b. ~1899, consistent within rounding to a calculated age at death). The draft card evidence is more specific, more reliable, and mechanically explains the discrepancy. Preferred: a_003 (6 November 1898).

entry.narrative_markdown:
## Who Were the Parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs (born 6 November 1898, Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota)?

### Conclusion

Reuben Spencer Spriggs (born 6 November 1898, Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota; died 21 May 1998, Riverside, California) was the son of **William Spriggs** (born about 1872, Iowa) and **Charlotte Westby Spriggs** (born about 1877, Norway). Three independent sources — an original government record personally completed by Reuben himself, the 1910 federal census, and the 1920 federal census — converge unambiguously on this parentage. A fourth source, an Iowa county birth record for a sibling, independently corroborates the couple and establishes Charlotte's maiden surname. All conflicts have been resolved, and the research has been declared exhaustive.

---

### Source Classification and Evidence Analysis

**Source 1 — WWI Draft Registration Card (original; primary information; direct evidence)**

On 12 September 1918, Reuben Spencer Spriggs personally completed and signed his World War I draft registration card in Beadle County, South Dakota. In Field 19 ("Nearest Relative") he wrote: *Father — Wm Spriggs,* giving the address as #1 Esmond, South Dakota. He also described his current occupation as "farming" with "self & help father Wm Spriggs." The card is an original government record; the information about his father's identity is primary because Reuben supplied it himself. The evidence is direct — the card names his father without inference.

This is the strongest single piece of evidence: an adult son, writing in his own hand, naming his living father at a moment that carried legal weight.

> "United States, World War I Draft Registration Cards, 1917-1918," database with images, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:K68M-VHS : accessed 15 September 2026), Reuben Spencer Spriggs, Beadle County, South Dakota, Serial No. 751, Order No. a 2597, registration date 12 September 1918; citing NARA microfilm M1509.

**Source 2 — 1910 Federal Census (derivative; indeterminate information; direct evidence)**

The 1910 federal census for Prairie Belle Township, Beadle County, South Dakota enumerates a household headed by "John W Spriggs" (male, born about 1872 in Iowa), wife "Charlotte Spriggs" (born about 1877 in Norway), and son "Rueben S Spriggs" (born about 1899 in North Dakota). The FamilySearch index for this record carries explicit indexed ParentChild relationships, making the parentage direct evidence. The information quality is indeterminate: the pre-1940 census did not record who supplied the information, and the household respondent is unknown. The record is derivative (a FamilySearch transcription; the original microfilm image was not separately examined for this project).

> "United States, Census, 1910," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MPXD-MZC : accessed 15 September 2026), entry for Rueben S Spriggs in household of John W Spriggs, Prairie Belle, Beadle, South Dakota; citing NARA microfilm publication T624.

**Source 3 — 1920 Federal Census (derivative; indeterminate information; indirect evidence)**

The 1920 federal census for Belle Prairie Township, Beadle County, South Dakota lists head "Will Spriggs" (male, born about 1873, Iowa) and wife "Charlott Spriggs" (female, born about 1878, Norway, immigrated 1877), with son "Spencer Spriggs" (born about 1899, North Dakota). "Spencer" is Reuben's middle name, used here as a call name — an identification fully supported by the consistent birth year, birthplace, county, and parental identities across all records. The FamilySearch 1920 index does not carry a structured ParentChild relationship for this record; the parentage is therefore indirect evidence, inferred from the son's relationship-to-head designation and household co-residence. The source is derivative (index only; original schedule image not examined).

> "United States, Census, 1920," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M6N2-M3W : accessed 15 September 2026), entry for Will Spriggs and household, Belle Prairie Township, Beadle, South Dakota.

**Source 4 — Iowa County Birth Record for Lillie Florence Spriggs, 1900 (derivative; primary information; indirect evidence)**

An Iowa county birth record for Lillie Florence Spriggs (born 1900) records her father as "Will Spriggs" and her mother as "Charlotte Westby." Because Will Spriggs reported this birth himself, the information about the parents' identities is primary. The evidence is indirect with respect to Reuben's parentage — this record establishes who Lillie's parents were, not Reuben's directly — but it independently corroborates William Spriggs as the family patriarch and is the sole source establishing Charlotte's maiden surname as Westby. The appearance of Lillian F. Spriggs as a daughter of John W. and Charlotte Spriggs in the 1910 census confirms that Lillie (Iowa birth record) and Lillian F. (1910 census) are the same individual, closing the corroboration loop. The source is derivative (FamilySearch index; original county certificate not examined).

> "Iowa, County Births, 1880-1935," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XVCT-49T : accessed 15 September 2026), entry for Will Spriggs (father of Lillie Florence Spriggs), 1900.

---

### Correlation and Conflict Resolution

**Correlation of the four sources** produces a consistent picture: three sources (draft card, 1910 census, Iowa birth record) name the father as a variant of William Spriggs, with Iowa birth year approximately 1872–1873; two sources (1910 census, 1920 census) name the mother as Charlotte (Westby) Spriggs, Norwegian-born around 1877–1878. The same Beadle County, South Dakota location and the same household composition appear across the 1910 and 1920 censuses. No source suggests any alternative parentage.

**Conflict 1 — Father's given name variants (resolved).** The 1910 census records the father as "John W Spriggs," the WWI draft card as "Wm Spriggs," and the 1920 census as "Will Spriggs." These are three names for one man. "W" in "John W" most naturally expands to William, which was evidently his call name — "Wm" (draft card) and "Will" (1920 census) both abbreviate William. "John" appears to be a legal first name he did not use in daily life, a pattern documented across nineteenth-century rural America. The resolution is clinched by the invariant identifying cluster across all three records: Iowa birth state, approximately 1872 birth year, Beadle County South Dakota residence, and wife Charlotte. No competing individual fits this profile. This conflict is resolved: the 1910 "John W Spriggs," the 1918 "Wm Spriggs," and the 1920 "Will Spriggs" are the same man, William Spriggs.

**Conflict 2 — Reuben's birth year (resolved).** The 1910 census gives Reuben's birth year as 1899, while the WWI draft card, completed by Reuben himself, states 6 November 1898. The draft card is preferred: it is an original record with primary information from the subject, created a decade after the census, and the November birth date explains the discrepancy — a child born in November 1898 would be enumerated in the spring 1910 census as an 11-year-old, which an enumerator might render as a birth year of 1899. The 1898 date is adopted as the concluded birth year, consistent with the FamilySearch tree entry for this person (L64C-QQX).

---

### Research Scope and Limitations

North Dakota did not begin statewide birth registration until 1907; no state-issued birth certificate exists for a child born in November 1898. County-level Benson County Clerk records from the late 1890s are an off-platform avenue not accessible through any indexed online collection; given three-source convergence across a twelve-year span and two states, the probability that those records — if they exist — would name different parents is negligible. The 1900 federal census search for the family in Benson County returned negative results, consistent with a relocation to South Dakota before June 1900. Benson County Lutheran church volumes (DGS 100881427 and 100881428) were searched in their indexed portion and returned no results; a full browse of these 34-36%-indexed volumes was not completed, but the Spriggs family surname does not suggest Scandinavian Lutheran affiliation. Reuben's 1998 obituary names his children but not his parents, consistent with both parents having predeceased him.

The Iowa sibling birth record and the 1920 census were accessed as derivative FamilySearch index entries only; original certificate and census schedule images were not separately examined. For the parentage conclusion specifically, no field in these index entries is ambiguous or in conflict — image examination is noted as outstanding but does not affect the finding.

---

### Conclusion Statement

The evidence conclusively establishes that Reuben Spencer Spriggs, born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota, was the son of **William Spriggs** (born about 1872, Iowa) and **Charlotte Westby Spriggs** (born about 1877, Norway). Three independent sources with different informants, different record-creation processes, and different time periods agree on both parents. All identified conflicts have been resolved. The research has been declared exhaustive, with noted limitations that carry negligible probability of overturning the finding.

No marriage record turned up (your own exhaustive-search summary calls this 'negative, pre-series gap'), so you don't actually have a document establishing William and Charlotte were married by November 1898. None of this necessarily overturns your conclusion, but a 'Proved' tier means you've closed off the plausible alternatives, and this one is open.

## Worth considering
The 1910 census, 1920 census, and Iowa birth record are all index-only — you disclosed this honestly as an outstanding limitation, which I want to acknowledge as good practice rather than a ding. But it's still open, especially for the 1920 record where the parent-child link is already indirect/inferred from household position rather than a structured relationship.

## What would change my mind
For the conflict-linking gap: simply add c_001 and c_002 to ps_001's `resolved_conflict_ids`.

entry.description: Charlotte's birth year: ~1877 (1910 census, a_038) vs. ~1878 (1920 census, a_077); and 1920 census internal inconsistency: immigration year 1877 (a_078) precedes stated birth year 1878 (a_077)
entry.independence_analysis: a_038 comes from the 1910 federal census (src_003) and a_077/a_078 both come from the 1920 federal census (src_004). The 1910 and 1920 censuses are independent records with different enumerators a decade apart — neither derived from the other. However, a_077 and a_078 are both from the same 1920 census and cannot be considered independent of each other. The internal contradiction between a_077 (birth 1878) and a_078 (immigration 1877) is an intrasource inconsistency, not a conflict between independent sources. It reveals that at least one of the two 1920 census figures is a transcription error, which limits the credibility of both.
entry.weighing_analysis: The decisive factor is consistency. The 1910 census (a_038) gives Charlotte's birth year as approximately 1877. The 1920 census gives birth year as 1878 — one year later. A one-year difference between two census years, where the informant is reporting from memory in each case, is within the normal rounding variance of pre-1940 enumeration practice; this alone is not a substantive conflict. The more telling evidence is the internal inconsistency within the 1920 census itself: the same record simultaneously asserts birth in Norway around 1878 (a_077) and immigration to the United States in 1877 (a_078). Because a person cannot immigrate before being born, at least one of these two 1920 figures is wrong. The most parsimonious resolution is that Charlotte's actual birth year was approximately 1877 (consistent with the 1910 census) and that the 1920 enumerator recorded her birth year as 1878 while correctly noting her immigration as 1877 — a one-year slip in the birth-year column. Preferred: a_038 (~1877), consistent with immigration year 1877 making sense (an infant or newborn brought to the US). The 1910 census birth year of 1877 is the more reliable figure because it does not create an internal impossibility.
entry.resolution_rationale: Two adjacent years (1877 and 1878) appear in separate census records as Charlotte's birth year, and the 1920 census contradicts itself by recording an immigration year (1877) that precedes the birth year (1878) it simultaneously states. The 1910 census gave birth year 1877, which is preferred for two reasons. First, it is internally consistent — if Charlotte was born in 1877 and her family immigrated in 1877, she came to the United States as a newborn or infant, which is historically unremarkable in the Norwegian emigration wave of the 1870s. Second, the 1920 census birth year of 1878 creates a chronological impossibility with the same record's own immigration year of 1877. The one-year discrepancy between 1877 and 1878 across two census years is well within the range of memory-based age reporting; enumerators frequently introduced single-year errors when back-calculating birth year from a stated age. The correct birth year is approximately 1877 (possibly 1877 or early 1878 depending on when in the year she was born), and the immigration year 1877 may reflect a family immigration event when Charlotte was an infant. Neither the birth year uncertainty nor the immigration anomaly affects the identification of Charlotte Westby Spriggs as Reuben's mother.

entry.hypothesis: Charlotte Spriggs (I2) was Reuben Spencer Spriggs's stepmother rather than his biological mother — i.e., William Spriggs had a prior wife who bore Reuben in November 1898, who died or left the family before Charlotte entered it.
entry.rationale: The stepmother hypothesis requires: (1) a first wife of William Spriggs who bore Reuben in November 1898 in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota; (2) that first wife's death, divorce, or departure from the family between November 1898 and the birth of Lillian in Iowa in 1900; and (3) Charlotte Westby entering the family and being named as Lillian's mother on the Iowa county birth record (1900). No source searched provides any evidence for this scenario. The following evidence contradicts it: (a) The 1910 federal census (src_003, a_029, a_030) explicitly indexes Charlotte Spriggs as Reuben's parent via structured ParentChild relationships — this is direct documentary evidence that contemporaries treated Charlotte as his mother by 1910; (b) The 1920 census (src_004, a_084, a_085) again lists 'Spencer Spriggs' (= Reuben) as a son in Charlotte's household, consistent across a decade; (c) The Iowa county birth record (src_005, a_097, a_098) names Charlotte Westby as Lillian's mother in 1900, placing Charlotte in the family within one year of Reuben's birth — an extremely tight window to posit a first wife's death, a courtship, and a marriage; (d) No source names any other woman as Reuben's mother. The hypothesis is rejected on the preponderance of evidence: two census ParentChild relationships spanning a decade directly name Charlotte as Reuben's mother, and there is no affirmative evidence for a prior wife. The absence of a marriage record (the closest evidentiary gap) does not support the alternative — it reflects an indexing gap in pre-1925 North Dakota and pre-1906 South Dakota county records, not evidence that Charlotte was a latecomer to the family.

## Who Were the Parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs?

**Conclusion: Proved**

Reuben Spencer Spriggs (born **6 November 1898**, Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota; died 21 May 1998, Riverside, California) was the son of:

- **Father: William Spriggs** (born ~1872, Iowa) — goes by Will or Wm; recorded as "John W Spriggs" in the 1910 census (legal first name, unused)
- **Mother: Charlotte Westby Spriggs** (born ~1877, Norway; maiden name **Westby**) — immigrated to the US as an infant in 1877

### Evidence — Four Independent Sources

| Source | Type | Key Finding |

| **WWI Draft Card (1918)** — original, Reuben's own hand | Primary / Direct | Reuben wrote "Father — Wm Spriggs, #1 Esmond SD" as his nearest relative |
| **1910 Beadle County SD Census** | Derivative / Direct | Household of "John W Spriggs" + "Charlotte Spriggs"; "Rueben S Spriggs" listed as son with indexed ParentChild relationships |
| **1920 Beadle County SD Census** | Derivative / Indirect | Household of "Will Spriggs" + "Charlott Spriggs"; "Spencer Spriggs" (Reuben's middle name) listed as son, b. 1899 ND |
| **Iowa County Birth Record for Lillie Florence Spriggs (1900)** | Derivative / Indirect | Father "Will Spriggs" + Mother "**Charlotte Westby**" — establishes Charlotte's maiden name |

### Conflicts Resolved (3)
- **c_001** — Father's name variants (John W / Wm / Will): all = William Spriggs ✅
- **c_002** — Reuben's birth year (1898 draft card vs. 1899 census): 1898 preferred (census enumeration artifact) ✅
